statement: Let G be a nonamenable discrete group. For every integer N ≥ 1 and every 0 < β < 1, there are finite nonempty sets X1, . . . , XN and Y0, . . . , YN−1, maps sk : Xk × Yk−1 −→ G, bk : G × Xk × Yk−1 −→ {E, F}, with the following properties. (F1) If k < N and bk(w; x, y) = E, then, with v = wsk(x, y), bk+1(v; x′ , y′ ) = E for every (x′ , y′ ) ∈ Xk+1 × Yk. (F2) For every k, w, x, #{y ∈ Yk−1 : bk(w; x, y) = F} |Yk−1| ≤ β. (F3) For every k, v, y, #{x ∈ Xk : bk(vsk(x, y)−1; x, y) = E} |Xk| ≤ β. 4 Each alphabet may subsequently be replaced by any positive integer number of copies, independently of the others, while preserving these properties. In particular, its cardinality can be made arbitrarily large and divisible by any prescribed positive integer.
